title: Hot Minute
essence: The finale. Haze gathers on the water and climbs, and everything the poet built, the city, the temple, the harbor, becomes weather; then it takes him last, from the feet up, while he resists. He floats again in the black of 01, but there are no walls this time, and his life flashes past as a reel of the suite's own motifs. Two of him dance and land the spin as a victory, and an old vintage door appears in the black. He opens it on a slow-motion party, the kind he once fell out of a window to escape, walks into the crowd, and the door closes.
palette_notes: Ascent blue #2560e1 (the poem's colour in film/poems.json) is the icy aerial Atlantis of 434b7bdd_1; the haze is blue-grey #8fa6b8 rising to near-white #d7dde2, taken from the fogged observation deck in 993cc7a2_0, not the orange of the haze district (orange is saved). The void is #050507 with a faint open horizon #1a1d2b. The single accent the film spends is the warm light under and through the door, #ffc46b; inside, the vintage party is amber #b5652e and wine #7a1f2b (a883ad75_3's warm blur, 01's party).

full_text.line: Don't make me leave and go where promises, hearts,
spectrums of light-filled constellations are broken.
I escaped here for a reason,
believing this would give me a sharpened key of answers
in a more grounded bravado
for my life of conquests and queries.
The way you see things felt safe and timeless.
Whatever has terminated this moment, damn you,
but let it feel love and lost as we must endure,
absent artificial escapes and machine learning strengths
for my highs and lows as resource materials.
Well, I can't leave behind the impulse
that comes from battle scars
and can't leave behind the wisdom that brushes gray tones
into our melanin after disappointments and defeats.
I trust that you'll be fine.
I escaped here for a reason.
Our dance together is a victory to entwine muses,
immersed in twisted dawns for a hot minute,
and a genesis of a New Testament as it ends.

insights: Use the same haze function for the city and for him: 'I have been weather before' only holds if it is literally the same mechanism.
Keep orange out of the haze; the warm door light is the one accent the film spends, and it lands harder if the whole poem before it is blue-grey and black.
NO WALLS is 01's black without the room: no rectangle anywhere, one open horizon, so the audience feels the difference from the opening poem.
The reel is the suite's own motifs and nothing else, each icon stopping at the noun; reuse the props built for 01-13 as flat insert cards rather than drawing new ones.
He exits through a door he chooses, not a window he falls through: keep the shut window visible in the party to say so.

Transcript correction from the treatment: 'twisted dons' is 'twisted dawns'. The reading departs from the treatment text elsewhere ('sharpened key of answers', 'gray tones into our melanin'); set the reading.

Atlas: 14 has no foundry frames; the archive's door-of-light (archive/925) and the red doors at the corridor end (views/006) carry the door beat. Build the door's light as a coded spill that pours toward camera along the floor ring, not a glow around the frame.
Atlas: re-grade the harbour wide to one orange ramp before the haze climbs; sodium light greys everything else, so the white temple goes grey last.
Atlas: the three figures on the catwalk are the same three cards in the party crowd; reuse them deliberately so the loop is legible.
Atlas: the Black has no line and no seam; keep every city detail (flood line, cyan seam, tide boards) out of 14.1-14.6.
future: This is the end. The door closing is the last image of the suite; the party and the door return the film to 01's slow party, so both poems should share the same party kit, garland and window.
The reel strip can serve as a title or credits device for the whole film.

atlas.district_language: Two districts and no geography. The Orange Haze (14.0) is low-pressure sodium: one orange wavelength that greys every other colour, so the harbour set is repainted in a single orange ramp from #fa8d15 down to #351106 and everything that is not orange reads grey. Silhouettes are small on catwalks and platforms over nothing; never a close-up outside. The haze is built as stacked translucent cards rising from the ground. Then The Black (14.1-14.6): no line, no seam, no floor, no walls. A black stage with the figure lit alone by one coded top light; the only architecture is the door. Its only colours are the flashing lights and then the warm amber leak of the vintage party under and around the door. Never draw a horizon line in the black except the one faint noise-bent strip the schema already has; never show the flood line or a cyan seam there.

staging.name: Taken by the haze
staging.shot: Wide: the harbour with everything he built as flat silhouette bands (Atlantis spires, the temple's white rise, the pier arm, a moored boat), all re-graded orange. Haze cards rise from the ground layer up through each band in turn; he stands at the rail of the platform at the catwalk's end. Slow tilt up his body as the haze climbs; close-up of his hand gripping the rail edge, stalling (reluctant_stall), then letting go.

staging.name: Floating in the black
staging.shot: Static locked frame, all black, the poet small centre frame, rotating slowly on a coded pivot, lit from above only. On 'terminated' the frame cracks: a white crack line card across the lens, held 6 frames.

staging.name: Cross-cut: highs and lows of life
staging.shot: Hard cuts on the beat between the floating poet and the reel's framed inserts (nine motif frames on a black film strip with sprocket holes, plus human B-roll). Each insert is a small rectangle in the black that slides through frame left to right.

staging.name: Battle scars and graytones
staging.shot: Macro along his forearm and cheek: a thin warm light line traces scar marks drawn on the puppet's skin card; the grade desaturates his costume card toward grey step by step.

staging.name: The vintage door appears
staging.shot: Wide: the old panelled door alone in the black, far, warm light under it. The poet enters frame from behind camera, his back to us, and walks to it. Faint ring of floor appears only around the door.

staging.name: The dance at the vintage party
staging.shot: Follow from behind through the slow-motion crowd: crowd as three depth layers of couple cards moving at 1/3 speed, paper-lantern garland overhead, gramophone on a side table, the dark shut window on the back wall. Then overhead: two dancers (the poet and POET_MUSE) under one spotlight disc on the floor.

staging.name: Disappears into the crowd; door closes
staging.shot: Hold on the back of the crowd as he walks into it and is lost among the couple cards. Reverse from the black: the open door, the amber party inside, the door swings shut toward camera, the light leak under it narrows to a line and goes out. END.

world_details.detail: the hot minute: when the Tide Engine's gates rise, every light in the city brightens for one minute; play it as all the windows and lamps in the harbour wide flaring together just before the haze takes them
the salt line at 4/10 of the catwalk rail's height, a pale stain on the rail
three figures walking the lit catwalk away from camera, the same three later dancing in the party
the chair at the foot of the stair, nobody ever sits in it

transitions.how: Dissolve by haze: white-out from the ground up, the Orange Haze arriving at the harbour; built from the same rising haze cards as 13.6.
The door closes on the viewer and the film loops: the closing door's light line becomes the first light of 01's black; the party behind the door is the party he fled through a window in 01.
